subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `cron.minInterval` as the operator-facing recurring-job cadence guardrail, with unset or `0` preserving current behavior and configured values rejecting or pacing fast schedules?
rationale: This adds a new core config surface and intentional configured fail-closed behavior for recurring cron schedules, which is a product and upgrade-compatibility choice beyond code correctness.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Fixes
options.body: Keep the config surface, require the generated docs-map fix and fresh exact-head proof, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.

options.title: Prefer Advisory Behavior
options.body: Reject enforcement for now and pursue a warning-only follow-up if maintainers want no schedule rejection or pacing behavior.

options.title: Defer Core Config
options.body: Pause this PR until the broader cron/session guardrail policy is split or settled in the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep the config surface, require the generated docs-map fix and fresh exact-head proof, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.
